headline: States pay Deloitte, others millions to comply with Trump law to cut Medicaid rolls
summary: Wisconsin faces approximately $10.2 million in state budget expenditures to upgrade Medicaid and SNAP eligibility systems for new federal compliance requirements, though the federal government covers 90% of development and 75% of maintenance costs. The state's budget is projected to realize $532.6 million in annual Medicaid spending reductions by removing an estimated 63,000 adults from coverage through new work requirements. These fiscal changes represent a significant shift in the state's financial priorities, trading upfront administrative investments for substantial long-term safety-net program cuts.
